arguments.value: Previously healthy adult woman presented with abrupt loss of consciousness, fever, rash/purpura, severe thrombocytopenia, shock, and acute multiorgan failure (CNS, liver, kidney) requiring ICU care, intubation, and vasopressors. Extensive initial CSF, infectious, and autoimmune workup was unrevealing; leptospirosis was later confirmed by positive IgM after exposure history suggested the diagnosis. Despite ceftriaxone, supportive care, and management of later MDR bloodstream/ventilator-associated infections, she developed persistent encephalopathy and ultimately died from multiorgan failure.
